source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Focus only on who made the final error, because workflow, staffing, technology, and environment do not affect safety events.","B":"Avoid examining system design after an error, because corrective actions should be limited to retraining one individual.","C":"Treat near misses as irrelevant to system learning, because only events that produce harm reveal process vulnerabilities.","D":"Examine workflow, staffing, technology, environment, and human factors to identify system contributors and safer redesign."}}
source_row.rationale: Modern patient-safety investigation uses systems analysis to identify workflow, staffing, technology, communication and human-factor contributors while still addressing individual accountability when appropriate.
source_row.source_detail: CANDOR Event Investigation and Analysis Guide emphasizes multidisciplinary systems analysis, contributing factors, human factors, process design and corrective actions rather than reflexive individual blame. AHRQ CANDOR Toolkit current module rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: AHRQ — CANDOR Event Investigation and Analysis
source_row.stem: After a medication error, the organization examines workflow, staffing, technology, communication and human factors in addition to individual actions. What safety approach is this?
